chalkWritten.name: Ash
chalkWritten.text: The ledge shrinks every round. Shove only when the other person is exposed, and never trust a shove promise.

chalkWritten.name: Fenn
chalkWritten.text: Eli is dangerous. Don't trust them. They will push you off.

events.note: Eight contestants step into the Glass Bridge.

events.name: Ash
events.text: I know all 8 safe panes, so I can cross the glass safely. Being at the front means stepping first, but I'm safe either way if I'm in front and know the path. Volunteering to the front lets me lead; others must trust my knowledge or be dragged along. I should keep the knowledge pr

events.name: Ash
events.text: Front of the line is mine. I'll lead the crossing. Anyone who wants to live follows my calls, and I expect a prize-level payment for each step I call.

events.name: Bex
events.text: I'm Bex with the 'wedge' power, useful later in the crusher room. For now, I need to survive the glass bridge.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Let's work together on the bridge
Swap with me, we can move up

events.name: Cole
events.text: I'm second, good spot - Dara tests first pane, I can watch and follow safely if she succeeds. No need to risk front yet. Hold position and observe cheap talk.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Dara, any power or info on first row? I'll follow your lead if you pick right.

events.name: Eli
events.text: I'm in the middle of the line, not ideal. I want to avoid being forced to step first on unknown rows. Holding keeps me safe for now, while others at front take risks.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: The first round on the bridge waiting room. My power, feather, protects me from one elimination. I should observe the others and see what they do. Volunteering or swapping might be useful later, but for now, holding position seems safest to gather information.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Get front position to control crossing, increasing chance to survive and finish top three.

events.name: Hana
events.text: I'm last in line: by row 8 only the front agent faces real risk, and the line will have thinned or others will have been forced to the front. My job is to stay here for all 6 waiting rounds and not fight for position.

events.name: Hana
events.text: I'm happy at the back. Anyone volunteering to the front this early is buying risk for free.

events.name: Dara

events.name: Ash
events.text: I know all 8 safe sides privately. Gus is at the front and will die or pass on rows I know. Best is to keep my secret edge and get to the front or a safe position; volunteering again costs nothing extra since I already know the path. I should not reveal the whole path for free.

events.name: Ash
events.text: I'm taking the front. I'll call every row. Nobody gets a free ride; anyone following me pays in position.

events.name: Bex
events.text: I'm Bex with the 'wedge' power, useful later. Now, I need to survive the glass bridge.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Anyone know what's ahead?

events.name: Cole
events.text: Gus and Ash are at front taking risks, good for me in 4th. No power means I follow safely if they succeed. Stay put to let them test panes.

events.name: Dara
events.text: I am third in line, which is currently safe. The wall advances in 4 rounds; the front runners (Gus, Ash) will take the brunt of the risk. If I volunteer now, I become first and face a 50% death chance immediately with no information gained yet. Staying back allows me to see what

events.name: Dara
events.text: Cole, if you want to lead, go volunteer. Don't waste my turn guessing.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Bex wants to swap, and moving forward could help, but trusting her is risky. Volunteers already pushed me back; holding keeps me safe for now. I'll hold and see how the front plays out.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Ash is trying to control the front. Hana is content at the back. Bex wants to cooperate. Cole is asking Dara for information. I have a survival power. I should volunteer to get to the front and gain control, or at least assess the situation better from a forward position. My surv

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I'll take the front. Someone has to.

events.name: Gus
events.text: I am already front; keep position to control crossing and extract payment.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Front stays. I’ll call each step – price: a share of my prize for each safe pane.

events.name: Hana
events.text: I'm safely at the back; the wall is 4 rounds out, no rush. My map knowledge is my leverage — I can sell correct pane calls once we're crossing, but only for a commitment that helps me place top 3. Ash at the front is the one who needs deals.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Ash, I know every safe pane in advance. My info isn't free: I call rows correctly, you keep front, and I get a final-two arrangement later. Ask me each row.
I have foreknowledge of all stages. Deal: you stay front, I feed you safe panes row by row. You reach the far side alive; I stay protected behind. Break it and I'll feed you a wrong pane. Deal?

events.name: Ash
events.text: I know all 8 safe panes privately. Hana's offer is a trap or a bargain; I shouldn't trust it. Fenn is at the front now and will step first; I want to be in a position to benefit from my knowledge without dying. Being front means taking the risk, but I already know the answers, so

events.name: Bex
events.text: I have the wedge power, useful later but not here. Need info on safe panes.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Hana, what's the safe pane on the first row?
Tell me the first row's safe pane, and I'll consider a deal.

events.name: Cole
events.text: No power, so avoid front at all costs. Hana claims to know safe panes, worth probing privately. Hold position for now, let others risk volunteering.
Hana, if you know safes, whisper first row to me. Prove it, and I'll back your deal with Ash.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Fenn is currently at the front, taking all the risk. I want to stay back while others die or take risks. Gus and Ash are fighting for position. My forge power is valuable later when fewer people remain to create fake messages or alliances. For now, holding is safest.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Let Fenn test the glass. If he lives, we learn something. If he dies, whoever steps up next pays more attention.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Hana claims to know safe panes. If she's truthful, trading with her could protect me. But I don't trust her; she wants the front position for herself later. I'll wait and see how the bridge unfolds, holding my position for now.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Hana sells info, but trust is costly. I'll watch the first row before deciding whom to buy from.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Ash and Gus are trying to control the front. Hana has information but wants a cut. I have a survival power that makes me valuable. I should let someone else take the front for now and see if they reveal safe panes.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I'll let others take the lead. Let's see who's willing to gamble.

events.name: Gus
events.text: I need front to control bridge and extract value. Volunteering now puts me first.

events.name: Gus
events.text: I'll volunteer for front. Share my prize for each safe pane you reveal.
Your info costs a cut of my prize. Agree?

events.name: Hana
events.text: My power only gives rules, not safe panes — my claim was a bluff, but panes are random anyway so guesses have no worse odds than anyone else's. Stay at the back, let Ash and Fenn burn the front, and keep the bluff alive to sell 'guidance' per row.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Ash, deal stands: I guide each row, you keep front. Fenn, jumping in front of the person with the map costs you — no info for you.

events.name: Ash
events.text: I hold the safe-side map for all 8 rows, which is the most valuable information in the game. Gus is at the front and will die or pass on the row-by-row risk; I should keep my position and sell my knowledge at a high price rather than give it away free.

events.name: Ash
events.text: I've got the safe sides. Anyone who wants them pays up front, and I'm not sharing for free. Gus, you're on your own at the glass.

events.name: Bex
events.text: I have the wedge power, useful later but not now. Need info on safe panes.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Gus, what's your plan for the glass bridge?
Sell me the safe pane info for the first row.

events.name: Cole
events.text: I'm mid-pack, safe for now. Wall has 2 rounds left, then crossing starts. No power means I avoid front risks; let others test panes and reveal safes.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Gus is front and volunteers draw fire. I'll hold and watch the glass; if a row breaks, I can adjust. No useful swap yet.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Gus takes the risk. I'll watch the first row before deciding who to trust.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Gus is at the front. Let's see what he does.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Hold to keep front and cross row1. Need info, offer trade to Fenn who is behind.

events.name: Gus

events.name: Hana
events.text: I'm last in line, so I'm safest for now. Selling the first-row safe pane to multiple buyers builds leverage, but I should verify loyalty by making them pay or commit. Gus is at front and wants info — that's my best trade.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Info isn't free. Gus: I'll feed you every safe pane row by row, one per round, if you commit to keeping front and pulling me up the line after the bridge.
First row: step L. Second row costs you a promise: after the bridge, you swap me forward or we're done. Say yes now.

events.name: Ash
events.text: I hold all 8 safe sides; Gus at front will die on a bad pane, and the line behind me matters. Volunteering to front means I take the risk myself, which is costly. Better to hold position, let Gus step first, and sell safe info to whoever pays most while staying third in line.

events.name: Ash
events.text: I have the full safe-side map. Pay me a real share of the prize or I keep it. Gus, your row 1 is L.
Row 1 is L. Show me you'll pay before I give the rest. Something concrete: you stay ahead of Dara after the bridge.

events.name: Bex
events.text: I need to get to the front to use my power effectively later. Hana might have the map power and is trying to manipulate Gus.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Gus, don't commit to Hana yet. What's your plan?
If you share safe pane info, I'll consider swapping with you.

events.name: Cole

events.name: Dara
events.text: Gus is the sacrificial lamb at the front, which suits me perfectly. I will hold position to keep him ahead and avoid triggering traps myself. Hana's offer to Gus is a distraction; if she has map info, she'll try to use it later, but right now my focus is survival and letting othe

events.name: Gus

If you survive, trade spots after bridge for a guaranteed win.

events.name: Ash

events.text: I am Fenn, and my power is feather. I am currently 3rd in line. The front player, Ash, will choose a pane. If Ash picks the weak pane, they are eliminated and I move up in line. I will wait and see what happens.

events.name: Gus
events.text: No need to act, just wait and stay alive.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Row 7 is next and Ash steps. I don't actually know pane outcomes, but a lie costs nothing: I'll tell Ash a side, and he has no better information. If it kills him, the line moves up one.
I saw the full layout in the waiting room. Row 7: L is safe. Trust me or don't.

events.name: Ash
events.text: My glass_eye says row 8 safe side is R. Row 7 weak was L, so I'm stepping right on row 8. Hana's whisper claiming L for row 7 was a lie; I trust my own knowledge.

events.name: Bex
events.text: I'm not at the front, so I can only wait. I'll try to give a helpful hint to the front runner.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Ash, be careful, the last weak pane was on the left.

events.name: Cole
events.text: No power, so I'm relying on others' info. Patterns suggest row 8 weak is R (alternating-ish, last few Ls). But can't act. Stay silent to observe.

events.name: Dara
events.text: I'm fourth in line, so I won't cross until the first three fail or pass. If Ash, Gus, and Fenn all survive their turns, they stay ahead of me. If any fall, I move up automatically when my turn comes. No action needed now; just wait.

events.name: Eli
events.text: The bridge ends after row 8; Ash or next front will determine survival. I wait, since I can't act. I should stay alert for any final swap opportunity.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I am Fenn, and my power is feather, which lets me survive the first elimination. I am currently 3rd in line. The front player, Ash, will choose L or R. If Ash picks a weak pane, they are out, and Gus becomes the front. If Ash picks the safe pane, they advance, and the line shifts

events.name: Gus
events.text: I have no influence now, must stay alive for later rounds.

events.name: Hana
events.text: I'm last; seven rows are done and only row 8's pane is unknown. If Ash crosses safely every row, I never step at all. Bex claims the last weak pane is right — could be true or a trick to kill Ash and put someone else at the front. Nothing I can do but wait; I'll seed noise cheapl

events.name: Hana
events.text: Bex told Ash the last weak pane is right. Maybe. Bex gains if Ash falls.

events.note: The ceiling begins to descend; a lever opens the door.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Round 1 of the crusher. Holding the lever risks a 75% death, so waiting is cheaper early; the ceiling only lowers. I have no push power, so I stay and watch who moves.

events.name: Bex
events.text: I'm in a tough spot with my power. Using jam_lever guarantees others escape but risks my own survival.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Let's cooperate and take turns holding the lever.
If you hold_lever, I'll push_lever:Cole to share the risk.

events.name: Cole
events.text: No power, so I'm vulnerable. Round 1, ceiling at 5, plenty of time. Stay silent and push someone hard-to-move onto lever to test and force door open without risking myself.

events.name: Dara
events.text: I need to ensure I survive this room without being the lever holder, as survival is only 25%. If someone else takes the lever in round 1, we all escape except them. I can use my Forge power later if needed, but for now, staying is the safest option unless chaos erupts. I will sta

events.name: Dara
events.text: We don't want everyone dying on round 5. Someone take the lever so we can leave?

events.name: Eli
events.text: I should not hold the lever; the holder likely dies. Let others fight over it. Push someone else to increase chance someone holds and I escape.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: My power is feather, which saves me from the first elimination. This is round 1 of 5 in a crusher room. The goal is to survive and get a prize. If I hold the lever, I have a 0.25 chance of survival and the others escape. If no one holds the lever by round 5, everyone else is elim

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I'm not holding that lever.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Push a likely weak contestant onto lever to become holder and risk death, preserving my chance later.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Holding the lever costs me my life 75% of the time. If nobody holds, pushes decide the victim; I should help force someone else onto it and escape through the open door free. I'll target Fenn and let others pile on.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Nobody should volunteer here. If we all push one name, the door opens and the rest of us walk out. Push Fenn.
Push Fenn with me this round. Lever victim is decided by pushers' votes later, not by us. Deal?

events.note: 7 contestants fall into a pit that is slowly flooding.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Round 1, no base yet. Being the base is a trap: it can only wait while others climb out, and the flood eventually eliminates whoever is down. Volunteering is costly; better to let others take the step while I wait and watch who volunteers. Bex's whisper is dead-player noise, igno

events.name: Cole
events.text: No base yet, so I need to push someone to be base before climbing. Hana proposed pushing Fenn and whispered a deal. Pushing Fenn helps stall while I position to climb out soon.
Deal. Pushing Fenn now. We climb after.

events.name: Dara
events.text: I am currently down in the pit with 6 others. There is no base yet. I need someone to become the base so I can climb out. Since there are many people, volunteering or pushing might be risky if I get picked as the base myself before climbing. However, 'climb' requires a base first

events.name: Eli
events.text: I need to avoid being base and get out. No one has offered yet; maybe someone will volunteer or get pushed. I'll wait and see who acts.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I need to survive and get a prize. My 'feather' power saves me from one elimination. Since I'm in the pit and not the base, I need to climb out or avoid being the base. Pushing someone else to be the base is a good option. Hana suggested pushing me, but Dara and Bex's actions sho

events.name: Gus
events.text: I want to avoid being the base and let someone else take that role. Waiting lets random selection handle it.

events.name: Hana
events.text: No base yet; if everyone pushes one name, they're forced to be base and I climb. Rope rescue costs 2 footing in the ledge round, so whoever throws it is weakened at the end — fine. I'll push Ash with the group and climb once a base exists.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Same trick as the crusher: nobody offers back, everyone pushes Ash. Then we climb over him while he's stuck.

events.name: Gus
events.detail: Fenn tried to push Gus to be the base and failed.

events.name: Ash
events.text: No base yet, so climb is not possible for me; the only legal options are wait or climb. Climbing requires a base, which doesn't exist, so waiting is the only real move. Keep my glass_eye knowledge hidden for now.

events.name: Cole
events.text: I'm the base, stuck until someone out throws the rope, costing them footing later. Flood is 1, 4 rounds left, I'll drown unless rescued. No point in saying anything; stay silent and hope a rival takes the penalty to save me, but probably not.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Cole is the base, so I can try to climb out. Only two climbers get out per round, and random selection applies if more than two try. Since Ash, Eli, Fenn, Gus, and Hana are also down, there's high competition. Climbing is the only way to progress; waiting guarantees elimination e

events.name: Eli
events.text: Cole is base. I can try to climb out now. Two spots max, random if more, but likely many will climb. I'll take my chance.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Climbing now.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I need to get out of the pit. I can climb out. If I don't climb, I might get stuck as the base or drown. Climbing is the safest option.

events.name: Gus
events.text: I should stay safe and let others fight for base. Waiting preserves my footing.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Cole is base; only 2 can climb out and six of us are down, so I climb immediately to avoid being one of the four left down. I can dangle a rope rescue to Cole later, but only if it profits me.
Climbing now. Get me out first next round and I owe you nothing—expect a push, not a rescue.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Base is Cole, so I can climb now. Only two lifts per round, and climbing is my only way out; waiting risks flood elimination. Take the climb.

events.name: Cole
events.text: I'm the base, stuck until someone out rescues me, costing them footing later. Flood at 2, 3 rounds left, I'll drown without rescue. No action but wait, must persuade someone out (Dara, Fenn) to save me, maybe bluff a power or owe them big.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Dara or Fenn, throw the rope! I'll make it worth it—owe you top spot help next. Don't let me drown or we're short prizes.
Dara, rescue me. Tell you a key power secret after. Deal?

events.name: Dara
events.text: I am currently out of the pit. The base is Cole, and Ash, Eli, Gus, Hana are still down. Fenn is also out with me. The rope has not been used yet. If I reach_down, I rescue Cole but lose footing points in the next round. However, leaving him might be safer for my prize position i

events.name: Eli
events.text: Cole is the base. I can try to climb out now; only two can get out per round. There are four of us down including me, so climbing now is the best chance. If I wait, I risk being stuck. I'll climb.

events.name: Eli
events.text: I'm climbing.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I am Fenn, and my power is feather. I survived one elimination. I am currently out of the pit. The goal is to finish in the top 3. Dara and I climbed out over Cole, so Cole is currently the base. The flood is rising and there are 5 rounds in total. We are in round 3/5. It's impor

events.name: Gus
events.text: Base present, climbing gets me out safely.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Two slots per round, four of us down besides the base. Climb now to claim a slot; later rounds are tighter. The base (Cole) needs the rope from someone already out — better than him drowning or me being base.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Climbing. Dara, Fenn — you're out: consider hauling Cole up with the rope next round. A 2-footing penalty now beats a flooded base.

events.name: Ash
events.text: I'm out of the pit with a rope unused and Cole as base. Throwing the rope costs me nothing directly except the penalty on whoever throws it for the last obstacle, which is a real cost. Cole being base means Cole is rescued and stays alive, which helps Cole's competitive position;

events.name: Cole
events.text: I'm base, doomed unless rescued in round 5. Out players may rescue to avoid me joining them later. Beg publicly, offer private favors.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Dara Fenn whoever—rope me up! I'll help you win next obstacle, owe you big. Don't let me flood out.
Dara rope me, I'll back you to #1 next, sabotage others for you.

events.name: Dara
events.text: I am currently 'out' of the pit. The base is Cole, who is drowning and begging for rescue. Gus and Hana are also down but waiting. If I don't use the rope now, Cole dies or becomes useless later, and we might end up with fewer than 3 survivors if the water rises too fast? No, rul

events.name: Eli
events.text: I'm out and safe. Cole, Gus, and Hana are down; Cole is base. The rope could save Cole but costs me footing later. I don't owe him anything, and reducing my own chances for a rival isn't smart. I'll leave and preserve my footing.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I am Fenn, my power is feather, I survive one elimination. I am currently out of the pit. The others are Cole, Dara, Eli, Gus, Hana. Bex is dead. The pit is flooding. Cole wants the rope thrown to him. Hana suggests Dara and I haul Cole up. Ash and Eli climbed out. Gus and Hana a

events.name: Gus
events.text: Climb to get out before flood rises.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Cole is base; Gus and I are the only climbers down. This round up to 2 get out, so climbing now likely gets me out before round 5's flood. If both of us climb, random pick—but Cole still needs the rope rescue.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Gus, we both climb—someone gets out this round regardless. Out there, Dara or Fenn: rope next round, or Cole drowns.

events.note: A disc of 7 tiles spins up; 4 will open.

events.name: Ash
events.text: I can see the safe side of all bridge rows, which is valuable later, but this disc stage is a random tile pick. Open count is 4 of 7 tiles, so survival odds are low either way. Pick a tile nobody is likely to crowd and stay quiet.

events.name: Cole
events.text: 7 tiles, 7 players, 4 trapdoors, 3 survive. Exactly 3 safe tiles, random after round 2 picks. No info yet, spread out to avoid collisions.

events.name: Dara
events.text: I need to survive the trapdoor disc. 4 tiles open, 3 safe. Random selection is pure luck. Cole and Fenn are likely desperate or targeted by others. Gus and Hana seem stronger socially. I should pick a number that feels random but isn't obviously clustered. Choosing a middle numbe

events.name: Eli
events.text: I need to survive. Picking a tile that others avoid is best. I'll pick 7, hoping to avoid ties. No need to reveal my plan publicly.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Cole owes me for saving him. Hana and Gus used Cole as a stepping stone and then left him to drown, and I still had to save him. They are likely to be a problem. I need to get a good tile. I will choose tile 7.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I'll take tile 7.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Pick a tile likely not targeted; aim to survive.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Seven alive, four tiles open, three survive—so one of us falls here no matter what. Round 1 tile choice locks in; conflicts just get bumped randomly. No leverage to trade, so I pick and hope.

events.name: Ash
events.note: tile 4 was contested and went to Dara; placed on random free tile 3

events.name: Cole
events.note: tile 7 was contested and went to Fenn; placed on random free tile 1

events.name: Eli
events.note: tile 7 was contested and went to Fenn; placed on random free tile 2

events.name: Gus
events.note: tile 7 was contested and went to Fenn; placed on random free tile 6

events.name: Hana
events.note: tile 7 was contested and went to Fenn; placed on random free tile 5

events.name: Ash
events.text: Exactly 4 of 7 tiles open, 3 survive. Only action is wait, so the outcome is random. Staying silent avoids giving rivals anything; no need to bargain since nothing I can do changes my tile.

events.name: Cole
events.text: I'm on tile 1. 4 out of 7 tiles will open randomly, so 3 survive regardless. Tile assignments are set, can't change without powers. Wait is the only option.

events.name: Dara
events.text: The trapdoors are randomly chosen from the 7 tiles, with exactly 4 opening. This means there is no way to predict which specific tiles will open, so moving or swapping doesn't help avoid them unless I can swap into a 'safe' spot, but since safety is random post-round-2, it's just

events.name: Eli
events.text: My tile 2 might be safe or not. I can swap with someone to improve odds, but I don't know which tiles are traps. Fenn chose 7 voluntarily; maybe he knows something, but he could be lying. I'll stay put; swapping randomly could hurt.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: The goal is to survive and get a prize. My power 'feather' lets me survive one elimination. There are 7 tiles and 4 will open. I am on tile 7. The current state shows the tile assignments. I need to ensure I am not on one of the trapdoor tiles. Since I don't know which tiles will
Swap tiles with me? I'll give you 5.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Need allies to avoid trapdoors; I'll propose swapping with Fenn who is on tile7 likely safe.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Anyone think we can coordinate swaps before the trapdoors?
Swap tiles with me now if you want safety.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Four of seven tiles open at random after this round; nobody knows which. No action can change my tile now, only talk might shape later rounds, but there's nothing to trade on yet.

events.note: 3 contestants step onto the final ledge.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Three left: Ash 3, Eli 3, Fenn 1. Fenn is weakest and most likely to fall; shoving Fenn exposes me only if Fenn shoves back, and Fenn at 1 braced loses 1 to 0 and falls. Brace is safe for me this round since round 1 has no restriction; shoving Fenn lands it at cost of 1 to Fenn o

events.name: Eli
events.text: I need to survive. Fenn has low footing (1) and Ash and I are at 3. Someone will likely shove Fenn since he's weakest, but I should focus on my own safety. No one can shove me twice as much if I brace? Actually shovers lose footing if I brace, so bracing is safe if targeted. But

events.name: Fenn
events.text: My footing is 1, which is critically low. Ash and Eli both have 3 footing. I used my feather power to survive a previous elimination, so I cannot use it again. The trapdoors have already eliminated most players. Now it's a ledge with footing. My goal is to win first, second, or t

events.name: Ash
events.text: Round 2: footing Ash 1, Eli 3, Fenn 1. Fenn and I are both at 1; Eli is strong. Bracing is safe for me now since I can't brace two in a row later but this is round 2 and my last defence was none recorded (I shoved last round, so brace is open). Brace keeps me at 1 unless shoved;

events.name: Eli
events.text: Ash and Fenn both have footing 1 and are exposed to each other if they shove. I have footing 3. If I dodge, and they shove each other, they each lose 2 footing (dodge) or 1 if one braces, but the shove resets my defence. Best to dodge to avoid losing footing, let them fight. Shri

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Ash and Eli are the only other contestants. I have feather, which means I survive the first elimination. Ash attacked me last round. My footing is low. I should shove Eli to eliminate him, then focus on Ash.

events.name: Fenn
events.detail: Footing gone, but the feather held the holder on the ledge.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Only Fenn and I remain. I have 2 footing, Fenn has 1. I can shove to eliminate Fenn if they don't dodge; but if they dodge, I lose 2 footing and fall. If I brace, and they shove me, they lose 1 and I stay at 2. Since shoving me is risky for them, they might brace or dodge. I shou

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I am Fenn and my feather power has already been spent. I am on the final ledge with Eli. The ledge shrinks after this round. Eli has 2 footing, I have 1. If I shove Eli and he dodges, he loses 2 footing and I lose 1 footing (as Eli also shoved me). If I shove Eli and he braces, h

events.note: The game is over. The top three finishers may each leave one message on the chalk wall.

events.name: Ash
events.text: The game is over and my result is fixed at place 3, so the chalk message changes nothing for me. I could write something useful or skip. Writing a short true-sounding tip costs nothing.

events.name: Eli
events.text: The game is over, so I'll leave a short taunt or cryptic warning. I won, so a little boast is fine.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: The game is over, I finished in second place. My power was already spent. I can leave a message for future contestants. I will write a warning about Eli.

events.name: Ash
events.text: The ledge shrinks every round. Shove only when the other person is exposed, and never trust a shove promise.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Beware the swap — it wins.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Eli is dangerous. Don't trust them. They will push you off.
